transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up time from people who have, you know, much more serious problems... but my regular doctor thought it might be good for me to talk to you. 

I came in because I just... I can’t seem to get anything in order anymore. It’s actually a bit embarrassing to admit, but my kitchen table is just covered right now. It has all my husband’s appointment papers, church flyers, notes from the senior center, and just... half-finished lists everywhere. I want to be organized, I really do, but I just sit there looking at it, not knowing which thing I should do first. And then somehow the whole day is just gone. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Do you find yourself having trouble focusing on tasks or activities outside of organizing your kitchen table as well?

Well... yes, I suppose I do. I hope that's not too unusual for someone my age. It's just little things, really. Like... if my husband has the television on in the next room, or if I'm at the senior center and two people start talking near me... my mind just sort of follows that instead. 

I certainly don't mean to eavesdrop or anything like that! It's just that my attention wanders over to whatever they're doing, and then I completely lose my place in what I was writing or planning. I try very hard to stay on track, I really do. I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is... is that the sort of thing you were asking about?
Do you often find yourself fidgeting or feeling restless when you're sitting still?

Oh, goodness... well, I suppose I do a little bit. I really do try my best to sit quietly and politely, you know, especially if I'm in a meeting at the church or the senior center. But I'll catch myself... well, rubbing my hands together, or tapping my foot. 

Sometimes I even click my pen without realizing I'm doing it. And I end up shifting around in my seat so much that... oh, it's a bit embarrassing to admit, but sometimes people actually look over at me. I always feel just terrible when that happens! I certainly don't want anyone to think I'm being rude or impatient with them. I just get this sort of nervous energy, I guess, and my body just wants to move. 

Is that... is that the kind of restlessness you mean, Doctor? I hope I'm answering your questions properly.
Have you been feeling anxious or overwhelmed by your difficulties with organization and focus?

Oh, well... I wouldn't say I'm terribly anxious. I really try not to let myself get too worked up over things, you know? It's just... well, maybe a little bit overwhelmed sometimes. 

I mean, I know I shouldn't complain. I have a lovely home and my husband is so good to me, so I really have no right to feel stressed. But when I look at all those papers and I just can't seem to make sense of them... I do get a sort of tight feeling in my chest. Just a little one! And I worry so much that I'm going to miss one of my husband's appointments or forget to pay a bill because I couldn't keep my mind on it. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound silly or dramatic. I know everyone gets a little behind sometimes. Do you think it's normal to feel a bit flustered about these sorts of things at my age?
Do you find yourself worrying about things even when there's no obvious reason to worry?

Oh, well... no, I don't think so. I mean, I really do try to look on the bright side of things. My husband always says I'm a bit of a worrywart, but I think that's just because I want to make sure everything is taken care of properly. 

I don't just sit around fretting about nothing at all, I promise! If I'm worrying, it's usually just about those silly papers or making sure I haven't forgotten something important for the house. I certainly don't want you to think I'm just an anxious old woman seeing shadows everywhere. I just want to be responsible, you know? Is that... is that the right way to think about it, Doctor?
Do you often feel guilty about things that wouldn't normally bother most people?

Oh, my... no, I really don't think I do. I mean, I certainly feel awful if I've actually let someone down or made a mess of things—like with my husband's papers, or if I forget to send a thank-you note. But just feeling guilty for no good reason, about things that shouldn't matter to most people? No, I wouldn't say I struggle with that. 

I always try my very best to do the right thing and be kind to everyone, so... well, I hope I don't have any reason to feel guilty like that! I just try to be a good, responsible person, you know. I hope that's the sort of answer you were looking for? I'm trying my best to explain it properly.
Do you tend to avoid tasks or activities because they feel too overwhelming or stressful?

Oh, goodness... well, I wouldn't say I intentionally *avoid* things. I always have the very best of intentions, I promise! But... I suppose I do have a bit of a silly habit of putting certain chores off. 

It's just that when there's a long form to fill out, or those dreadfully complicated insurance papers to read through, or even just trying to put together a program schedule... I keep finding little reasons to do something else first. I'll tell myself I absolutely must tidy the kitchen or water the plants before I can sit down and focus on it. 

I feel a bit ashamed to admit it, but my head just feels so worn out before I even start. I look at the paperwork and I just feel so drained all of a sudden. I hope you don't think I'm just being terribly lazy, Doctor. I really do try my hardest to get to them eventually. Do you think it's alright that I need to pace myself with things like that nowadays?
Do you often interrupt others when they're speaking?

Oh, goodness, no! I certainly hope I don't do that. I was always taught it's terribly rude to interrupt when someone else has the floor. 

I really do try my very best to be a good listener. Sometimes, I suppose, if I get very excited about a topic or if I'm worried I might forget a thought I just had, I might accidentally speak up a little too soon. But I always apologize right away if I do! I never want anyone to feel like I don't care about what they have to say. 

I pride myself on being polite, you see. I would feel just awful if people thought I was one of those pushy sorts who just talks over everyone. I haven't been doing that with you today, have I, Doctor? I'd be so embarrassed if I had been interrupting you without realizing it!
Do you often blurting out answers before questions have been completed?

Oh, dear me, no. I really try my hardest to wait my turn. It's just basic good manners, isn't it? To let someone finish their sentence before you chime in. 

I mean, I suppose there might be times when I'm just so eager to help, or I think I know exactly what someone is going to say, that a little word might slip out... but I certainly don't make a habit of it! I would hate to come across as impatient or disrespectful. 

I always want people to feel heard and respected when they talk to me. I hope I haven't been doing that to you, Doctor? Jumping the gun, I mean. I really do try to be patient and listen properly, I promise.
Are you having difficulty completing daily tasks or responsibilities due to your troubles with organization and focus?

Oh, goodness... well, I suppose things have gotten a little bit trickier lately, though I really do try my best to keep on top of everything. I don't want to sound like I'm completely falling apart, because I'm not! I still manage quite a bit on my own.

But... well, I did step down from leading the big spring gala at the senior center this year. I just told everyone I wanted to give the younger folks a chance to take the reins, which is true! But... if I'm being perfectly honest, and I know I should be honest with you, it was just getting to be too much to juggle. All the details and schedules... I was so afraid I'd mess it up and ruin it for everyone. 

And... oh, this is a little embarrassing to admit... my daughter, bless her heart, she's started double-checking my bills and my calendar. She says she just wants to help her old mom out, but I know it's because she's noticed I've mixed up a few due dates and missed a doctor's appointment or two recently. I feel terrible that she feels she has to check up on me like that. I don't want to be a burden to her. 

It's just that it takes me so much longer to sort through the mail and figure out what needs doing, and by the time I try to organize it all, my mind just goes fuzzy. Do you think it's normal for things to slip a little bit at my age, Doctor? I really am trying my hardest to stay independent.
Do you have difficulty waiting for your turn in lines or when doing activities with others?

Oh, heavens no. I actually don't mind waiting my turn at all. I... well, I was always taught that patience is a virtue, you know? So if I'm at the grocery store or waiting at the pharmacy, I just stand quietly. It's really no trouble. 

I'd never want to cause a fuss or make anyone else feel rushed. That's just part of being polite and living in a community, don't you think? I certainly hope I come across as a patient person. I would be absolutely mortified if anyone ever thought I was being demanding or, heaven forbid, trying to cut in line. I'm quite happy to just wait until it's my time. That is the right way to behave, isn't it, Doctor?
Have you noticed any problems in your relationships with family or friends due to your difficulties with organization and focus?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say there are any real problems. My family and friends are just wonderful, they really are. We all get along so beautifully. 

I suppose... well, sometimes I might forget to call someone back right away, or I might get a little mixed up about what time we're supposed to meet for lunch. But they know I don't mean any harm by it! They're always so forgiving. 

My daughter... well, like I mentioned, she helps me out a bit now, but we never argue about it. She's just being sweet. I always try to make sure I'm doing my part to keep everyone happy and not be a bother. I'd hate to think my little slip-ups were causing any real friction. Relationships are so precious, aren't they? I do everything I can to keep mine running smoothly. I hope that sounds like I'm managing things alright?
Do you often talk more than others in social situations?

Oh, goodness, no. I really try my best to be a good listener. I was always taught that it's impolite to monopolize a conversation, so I make a point to let others have their say. 

If anything, I'm probably the quiet one in the group! I just love hearing what everyone else has been up to, especially my friends from the garden club. I'd never want anyone to think I was self-centered or talking their ear off. That would be so rude, wouldn't it? I always try to make sure I'm asking questions and showing interest in them. I think that's the polite way to socialize, don't you agree, Doctor?
Do you feel like your difficulties with organization and focus are affecting your overall quality of life?

Oh, goodness, I wouldn't want to complain. I really do have a lovely life, I truly do. I'm very blessed. 

But... well, I suppose if I'm being perfectly honest, I have had to make a few little adjustments lately. Just to keep things pleasant for everyone, you know? Like, um, I used to lead this wonderful, big event at the senior center, but I recently had to give it up. I just... I didn't want to risk letting anyone down if I couldn't keep all the details organized. It's much better to step aside before you become a burden to the group, don't you think? 

And... oh, it's a little embarrassing to admit, but my daughter has actually started double-checking my bills and my appointments for me. I think... well, she just doesn't quite trust that I can keep everything straight on my own anymore. I hate making her worry like that. But I just let her do it, because I want to be agreeable and give her peace of mind. Accepting help gracefully is the right way to handle it, isn't it, Doctor? I certainly hope I'm doing the right thing.
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that at all. I've always tried to be very careful and deliberate about things. Acting out like that... well, it just wouldn't be very ladylike, would it? 

I always try to take a moment to think before I do anything. I wouldn't want to make a rash decision and cause a fuss or inconvenience anyone. If there's a big choice to be made, I usually ask my daughter for her thoughts anyway, just to be sure I'm making the sensible choice. I think it's always best to be cautious and considerate, don't you? I'd hate for anyone to think I was being reckless or unpredictable. That's not me at all, Doctor, I promise.
Do you often find yourself dominating conversations or having trouble letting others speak?

Oh, my, I believe we just touched on that, didn't we? I hope I wasn't being confusing before. No, I really don't do that. I'd be mortified if I ever dominated a conversation. 

I was always raised to believe that a conversation is a two-way street, you know? It's so important to let everyone have their turn. I would never want to make anyone feel like their thoughts weren't valued. If anything, I'm usually the one asking all the questions so the other person can shine. That's the gracious way to handle a chat, don't you think? I certainly try my best to be polite like that.
Have you experienced significant difficulties with inattention or hyperactivity-impulsivity since childhood?

Oh, my... well, childhood feels like such a very long time ago, doesn't it? I was always a very happy little girl, truly I was. I loved school and my teachers were always so sweet to me. 

But... well, I suppose if I think back to my report cards... oh, it's a bit silly to bring up now, but my teachers used to write that I was a bright girl, which was lovely of them to say, of course. But they also said I could be a little... well, they used the word "careless." I didn't mean to be, I promise! I just... I was always forgetting my books or my homework assignments. And they would have to give me little reminders to finish my seatwork before I was allowed to go outside and play. I always felt so terrible when they had to remind me. I just wanted to be a good student for them, you know? It's perfectly normal for children to be a little forgetful sometimes, though, right, Doctor? I hope it doesn't make me sound like I was a naughty child.
Have you experienced significant difficulties with inattention or hyperactivity-impulsivity as an adult?

Oh, goodness, no. I really wouldn't say I have significant difficulties... that sounds so terribly serious, doesn't it? As an adult, I've always tried my very best to be responsible and keep things running smoothly. I certainly wouldn't want to be a burden on anyone.

I mean, of course, everyone misplaces their keys now and then, or forgets why they walked into a room. That's just a normal part of getting older, isn't it? My daughter helps me keep track of the important things, like my appointments and such, which is so very sweet of her. I do try to stay organized, I really do. Sometimes I might start a little project, like sorting through old photographs, and... well, maybe I get a bit distracted and don't quite finish it right away. But I always mean well, and I never want to cause any trouble. That's just ordinary forgetfulness, right, Doctor? Nothing to be overly concerned about, I hope.
Have you consistently struggled with staying focused or following through on instructions throughout your adult life?

Oh, my... consistently struggled? Well, I don't know if I'd use the word "struggled," Doctor. That sounds like I'm not trying very hard, and I promise you, I've always tried my absolute best to be diligent and helpful. I would hate for you to think I was lazy or uncooperative.

I suppose... well, maybe I'm just a little scatterbrained sometimes? Like, if my husband used to give me a list of things to pick up at the market, or if I'm trying to follow a new recipe, I might... I might miss a step here or there. But I always mean to do it perfectly! It's just that my mind sort of wanders, or I get caught up thinking about something else, and then... oh, goodness, I realize I've completely lost the thread of what I was doing. But it's not on purpose, I assure you. And I do eventually get things done, even if it takes me a little longer than most people. That doesn't make me a bad person, does it? I think everyone gets a little turned around with instructions sometimes, wouldn't you agree?
Did you have difficulty paying attention or following instructions as a child?

Oh, dear... well, I suppose you did just ask about my childhood a moment ago, didn't you? I hope I answered it properly the first time. I really don't want to waste your time or make you repeat yourself, Doctor. 

As I was saying before, I was such a happy little girl, and I always wanted to please my teachers. I don't remember having any real trouble paying attention... at least, not any more than any other child would. Sometimes the lessons were just a little long, and it was so lovely outside. I might have daydreamed just a tiny bit, but I never disrupted the class or anything dreadful like that. And if I missed an instruction, well, I think it was just because I was so eager to get started on my work that I perhaps didn't listen to the very end of what the teacher was saying. But I was always a good girl, I promise. You don't think a little daydreaming means there was something terribly wrong with me back then, do you?
